newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX spot crude slips below $19.00 on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX spot crude slips below $19.00 on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX spot crude slipped below $19.00 a barrel in Friday afternoon trade for the first time in over a year after weakness on London's IPE triggered a strong bout of technical selling, traders said.
"We broke several support levels, the first one being $19.35 which corresponded to what was going on with Brent over in London," said New York crude trader.
At 1451 EST, May crude was off 37 cents at $19.10 but fell to a session low of $18.96, its lowest point since March 4, 1996 when it fell to a session low of $18.78.

"We found good support near $18.95," said the crude trader. Pegasus Econometric Research noted channel support on crude's spot continuation chart at $18.80, created by a the descending trendline that extends through the low March 3 of $19.96 and on the upper end, from the high January 31 of $25.00.
May Brent was off 50 cents at $17.67 a barrel on London's IPE, a new nine-month low.
The previous support of $19.35 for NYMEX May crude was created by this past Tuesday's session low and was the lowest point for spot crude since March 11, 1996.
Caught under crude's downdraft, May gasoline was off 0.30 cent at 60.60 cents a gallon while May heating was off 0.26 cent a gallon at 53.00 cents.
